rows.question: Identify a list of genes expressed in lung cancer
rows.pred_sql:
WITH healthy_expression_by_anatomy AS (
  SELECT
    ensembl_gene_id,
    uberon_anatomical_id,
    expression_score
  FROM healthy_expression
),
xref_ensembl_to_symbol AS (
  SELECT
    ensembl_gene_id,
    gene_symbol
  FROM xref_gene_ensembl
  WHERE ensembl_gene_id IS NOT NULL
    AND ensembl_gene_id <> ''
),
differential_expression_rows AS (
  SELECT
    gene_symbol,
    doid
  FROM differential_expression
  WHERE gene_symbol IS NOT NULL
    AND gene_symbol <> ''
)
SELECT DISTINCT gene_symbol
FROM (
  -- genes from differential_expression linked to diseases with 'lung' in the name
  SELECT der.gene_symbol
  FROM differential_expression_rows der
  JOIN disease d ON der.doid = d.id
  WHERE d.name ILIKE '%lung%'

  UNION

  -- genes from healthy_expression where tissue maps to cancer_tissue for diseases with 'lung' in the name
  SELECT x.gene_symbol
  FROM (
    SELECT he.ensembl_gene_id
    FROM healthy_expression_by_anatomy he
    JOIN cancer_tissue ct ON he.uberon_anatomical_id = ct.uberon_anatomical_id
    JOIN disease d ON ct.doid = d.id
    WHERE d.name ILIKE '%lung%'
    GROUP BY he.ensembl_gene_id
    HAVING MAX(he.expression_score) IS NOT NULL
  ) he_genes
  JOIN xref_ensembl_to_symbol x ON he_genes.ensembl_gene_id = x.ensembl_gene_id
  WHERE x.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL
    AND x.gene_symbol <> ''
) s
ORDER BY gene_symbol

rows.question: What are the name of cancer types where the A1BG gene expression is significantly increased (up regulated)
rows.pred_sql:
WITH de_up AS (
  SELECT
    de.gene_symbol,
    de.doid,
    de.log2fc,
    de.pvalue,
    de.adjpvalue,
    de.statistical_significance,
    de.expression_change_direction
  FROM differential_expression de
  WHERE
    de.gene_symbol = 'A1BG'
    AND (
      lower(coalesce(de.expression_change_direction, '')) IN (
        'up','increased','up-regulated','upregulated','increased expression','up regulated','upregulated','positive'
      )
      OR lower(coalesce(de.expression_change_direction, '')) ~ '^(up|increase|up[\\s\\-]?regulat)'
    )
    AND (
      (de.adjpvalue IS NOT NULL AND de.adjpvalue <= 0.05)
      OR (de.adjpvalue IS NULL AND de.pvalue IS NOT NULL AND de.pvalue <= 0.05)
      OR lower(coalesce(de.statistical_significance, '')) IN ('significant','yes','true')
    )
)
SELECT
  d.name AS disease_name,
  d.id AS disease_id,
  de.log2fc,
  de.adjpvalue,
  de.pvalue,
  de.expression_change_direction,
  de.statistical_significance
FROM de_up de
JOIN disease d ON d.id = de.doid
ORDER BY de.log2fc DESC

rows.question: Get the biomarker gene symbol and biomarker description for disease with name 'breast cancer'
rows.pred_sql:
WITH target_disease AS (
  SELECT id AS doid
  FROM disease
  WHERE name = 'breast cancer'
)
SELECT
  b.gene_symbol,
  b.biomarker_description
FROM biomarker b
-- No direct biomarker -> disease table exists in the schema. However some tables reference doid:
-- biomarker_fda_test.doid, differential_expression.doid, disease_mutation.doid, cancer_tissue.doid, etc.
-- To remain inclusive, return biomarkers that are linked to 'breast cancer' via any table that references doid
-- and also links back to biomarker either directly by id or via FDA test tables.
-- We'll consider two reasonable linkage paths present in the schema:
-- 1) biomarker_fda_test.test_submission / biomarker_fda.test_submission join to biomarker_fda to biomarker_fda_ncit_term/biomarker_fda_drug isn't directly linked to biomarker table.
-- 2) There is no explicit FK from biomarker to those tables. Given schema lacks a clear join, restrict to biomarkers
--    that have the disease's doid appearing in biomarker_fda_test.doid and then include biomarkers whose id matches
--    ncit entries in biomarker_fda_ncit_term or drugs in biomarker_fda_drug is not reliable.
-- Because no unequivocal linking path exists in the schema, return biomarker rows only when there exists at least one
-- table row that connects that biomarker.id to the disease.doid. The only table that contains a biomarker id column is
-- biomarker_alias, biomarker_article, biomarker_edrn, biomarker_fda, biomarker_fda_test (via test fields), and biomarker_fda_* tables.
-- Of these, biomarker_edrn.id and biomarker_fda.id could match biomarker.id. We'll use those possible joins.
LEFT JOIN biomarker_edrn be ON be.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda bf ON bf.id = b.id
LEFT JOIN biomarker_fda_test bft ON bft.test_submission = bf.test_submission
LEFT JOIN target_disease td ON
  td.doid = bft.doid
WHERE td.doid IS NOT NULL
